I fixed every rule in `pricebook.py` whose behavior didn't match its docstring. Afterwards I re-checked all 150 rules against their docstrings and the module-level common rules, using a wide range of quantities and unit prices, and none differ any more.

**Rules whose results were actually wrong (10):**

| Rule | Problem | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| 35 | Capped the discounted amount instead of the discount | Now caps the discount |
| 93 | Capped the base price instead of the discount | Now caps the discount |
| 102 | Capped the base price instead of the discount | Now caps the discount |
| 45 | Rounded the discount with `round()` instead of flooring | Changed to `// 100` (floor) |
| 57 | Rounded the discount with `round()` instead of flooring | Changed to `// 100` (floor) |
| 115 | Rounded the discount with `round()` instead of flooring | Changed to `// 100` (floor) |
| 66 | Applied 3% instead of the documented 2% | Now 2% |
| 83 | Applied 8% instead of the documented 7% | Now 7% |
| 105 | Documented as marginal but discounted every unit (whole) | Now discounts only units above the threshold |
| 107 | Documented as whole but discounted only units above the threshold (marginal) | Now discounts every unit |

**Wrong threshold in code, same results (2):** in rules 39 and 43 the code started the discount at 6 and 21 units instead of 5 and 20. For these rules the discount is 0 at exactly the threshold quantity anyway, so prices never changed. I still set them to 5 and 20 to match the docstrings.

STATUS: DONE
